resources.string: Knee, hip and shoulder angles, left vs right
Phone at hip height, 2–3 m away. Stand side-on so the camera sees one side; you will turn round for the other.
Phone at chest height, 2–3 m away. Face the camera with both arms in view.
Move slowly to the end of your comfortable range and hold still for about a second. The tool keeps the highest angle you hold still, beeps, and then asks for the other side.
Typical error ±10° (side-view knee, checked against a lab measurement). Compare with yourself in the same setup; it is not a clinical goniometer.
Hip and shoulder angles have no reference measurement yet. Expect at least the knee\'s ±10° error and compare only with yourself.
Phone at hip height, 2–3 m away, facing you. Stand on one leg with both feet in view.
Lift one foot clearly off the floor. The clock starts after 0.3 s and stops when the foot touches down, the hips sway too far or you leave the picture; 60 s at most.

Sway is the average hip movement in % of leg length; sway speed is the hip path per second above the noise measured while you stood still. Both include the pose model\'s own jitter, so compare with yourself on the same phone and distance.
Repeat on the other leg to compare left and right.
Tripod at the finish line, camera looking across it; the line is the band in the middle of the picture. The athlete starts on the beep.
Tripod at the line, camera looking across it. The time runs from the first crossing to the next one (out and back, or a lap).
Enter a distance from 1 to 400 m.
Tripod at the timing line, 5 m before the turning line. Run in through the line, turn and run back through it.
Tripod at the start/finish line of the T. The time runs from leaving the line to coming back through it.
Phone 2–3 m away facing you, held still. Wait for the tone and move as fast as you can.

Times come from the camera frames, so they are exact only to one frame (about 33 ms at 30 fps), shown with each result. The leading arm or leg may cross before the torso. Real timing needs a real phone on a tripod.
Includes the phone\'s audio delay, which is not measured (often 20–150 ms), and one frame of camera timing. Compare with yourself on the same phone.
Side-on to the camera. Move to your end range and hold still.
Face the camera. Raise the arms sideways and hold still.
Face the camera, stand still on both feet for a second, then lift one foot.
Stand still and react to the tone.
Press Start; on the beep the athlete runs through the line.
Press Start; the clock runs from the first crossing to the next.
Keep the phone still. The orange band is the timing line.
Now turn round to show the other side
Move to the end of the range and hold still
No still hold yet. Hold the end position for a second.
Lift one foot off the floor
Running: waiting for the finish crossing
False start: movement before the tone. Try again.
No finish detected in time. Try again.
Stay still… wait for the tone
Left–right difference %1$s: within the measuring error
Left–right difference %1$s: larger than the measuring error
Only one side was held still; repeat to compare left and right.
Sway speed %1$s%% of leg length per second above the still noise (%2$s%%/s)
Sway speed %1$s%% of leg length per second; the still noise was not measured (stand still on both feet for a second before lifting)
Started on the phone\'s tone: includes the reaction and the phone\'s unmeasured audio delay.
Started when the tone left the phone\'s audio output (measured by the phone): the time includes your reaction and the sound\'s travel to you.
This camera\'s frame clock is only roughly aligned with the phone clock; cue-started times are less exact.
Only the summary is saved: distance, time, pace and kilometre splits. The route stays on this phone.
Distance, pace and splits from the phone\'s location. Recording continues with the screen off.
GPS readings drift by a few metres: fixes worse than 25 m are skipped and standing still adds nothing, so short distances read slightly low. Needs a real phone outdoors.
You can lock the screen; the notification shows the recording and has a Stop button.
Location permission is needed to record distance.
